title: darrylmorley/whatcable
claim: darrylmorley/whatcable — macOS menu bar app that tells you, in plain English, what each USB-C cable plugged into your Mac can actually do
why_good: Solves the everyday USB-C guessing game — which cable does 100W? 40Gbps? — right in the menu bar; a real annoyance with a clear, narrow scope.
value: A cheap paid Mac utility (one-time or small subscription) for pros with drawers of identical-looking cables; expand into a cable-identifier database.
risk: Tiny scope and easily cloned; Apple could surface this natively and free alternatives can appear fast.

zh.claim: darrylmorley/whatcable —— macOS 菜单栏 app,用大白话告诉你插进 Mac 的每根 USB-C 线到底能干什么(供电/速率)。
zh.why_good: 解决 USB-C 的日常猜谜——哪根线能 100W?40Gbps?——直接在菜单栏给答案,痛点真实、范围清晰。
zh.value: 给一抽屉长得一样的线的专业用户卖个便宜的 Mac 小工具(一次性或小额订阅),再扩成线材识别数据库。
zh.risk: 范围小、易被抄;Apple 可能原生做掉,免费替代也会很快冒出来。
zh.hook: 家里抽屉全是长得一样的 USB-C 线的人——Mac 用户已经在为 Pro 授权付费、主动提交诊断数据，就为搞清哪根线支持 100W 或 80Gbps。
zh.does: macOS 菜单栏 app，用大白话读出每根插入的 USB-C/雷电线实际协商到的能力——功率、速率、代际。亮点：社区共建的线缆能力数据库，求助帖里几十位用户主动提交自己 Mac 的 ioreg 数据。
zh.gap: 能力数据只存在于英文、Mac-only 的菜单栏应用里；中文市场——杂牌线乱标问题严重得多——以及 Windows/Android 侧没人做。
zh.counter: 工具盘子太小、开源且极易被克隆；Apple 只要在系统设置里原生显示线缆协商信息，这个品类一夜归零。
zh.differentiator: 做中文版＋国产品牌线缆实测库（绿联/安克/小米），检测核心直接复用开源实现；手机快充场景是扩展方向。
zh.consumer_angle: 本身就是消费级产品：用大白话回答“哪根线是好线”，按廉价 Mac 工具出售。

hook: Anyone with a drawer of identical USB-C cables — Mac users already pay for Pro licences and mail in diagnostics just to learn which cable does 100W or 80Gbps.
pick_reason: Addresses a common consumer pain point with a clear product that can be monetized.

voices.quote: Caldigit TS3 Plus (docking station, TB3) and ACASIS TBU405Pro (mobile hard drive, TB4) only support 40Gbps but be marked "can do 80Gbps" when connected to M4Max Studio's back ports
Just submitted my M4 Mac mini diagnostic data. I plugged in my hub and a bunch of devices that are currently working, so hopefully it helps a bit.

does: macOS menu bar app that reads what each plugged-in USB-C/Thunderbolt cable actually negotiates — wattage, data speed, generation — in plain English. Standout: a community-fed capability database; its help-wanted data threads draw dozens of users submitting ioreg dumps from their own Macs.
gap: The capability data lives in an English, Mac-only menu bar app; the Chinese market — where mislabeled third-party cables are far worse — and Windows/Android have nobody doing this.
counter: Tiny utility scope, open source and trivially cloned; Apple could surface cable negotiation natively in System Settings and end the category overnight.
differentiator: Chinese-market version with a tested database of domestic-brand cables (绿联/安克/小米 实测库), reusing the open-source detection core; phone fast-charging scenarios as the expansion.
consumer_angle: Already a consumer product: plain-English answers to 'which cable is the good one', sold as a cheap Mac utility.
